# Container & VM Isolation for Agent Workspaces

Isolation mechanisms for running AI coding agents safely, from lightweight containers to hardware-enforced microVMs.

## Technology Comparison

| Technology | Isolation Level | Boot Time | Memory Overhead | Syscall Coverage | Best For |
|-----------|----------------|-----------|-----------------|------------------|----------|
| Docker (rootful) | Process (shared kernel) | <100ms | ~80-150 MB daemon | 100% | Trusted workloads [1] |
| Podman (rootless) | Process + user namespace | <100ms | No daemon | 100% | Trusted-but-risky workloads [24] |
| gVisor (runsc) | User-space kernel | <100ms | Medium | ~70-80% | Multi-tenant SaaS, CI/CD [2][4] |
| Firecracker | Hardware (dedicated kernel) | ~125ms | <5 MiB/VM | Limited but sufficient | Untrusted code, serverless [2][3] |
| Kata Containers | Hardware (via VMM) | ~200ms | Higher | ~100% | Regulated industries, K8s [2][5] |
| E2B | Firecracker-backed (cloud) | 80ms | Managed | Full | Rapid prototyping, managed [32] |
| Daytona | Docker default, Kata optional | <90ms | Varies | Full | AI code execution infra [46] |

## Podman Rootless

The reference implementation (`dev-and-ai-tools`) uses Podman rootless [43]. Key security properties:

- **No daemon**: Fork-exec model eliminates the privileged daemon attack surface present in Docker [24]
- **User namespace**: Container escape yields only the invoking user's UID, not root [24]
- **Fewer default capabilities**: Podman exposes 11 capabilities vs Docker's 14 (discovery)
- **CVE posture**: runc CVE-2024-21626 impact is reduced — rootless means runc itself runs unprivileged (discovery)

Practical hardening flags [24][43]:

```bash
podman run \
  --cap-drop ALL \
  --security-opt no-new-privileges \
  --network none \
  --memory 4g \
  --cpus 2 \
  --pids-limit 50 \
  --read-only \
  --tmpfs /tmp:size=100m \
  -v "${WORKTREE_ROOT}:/workspace:z" \
  -v "${AUTH_DIR}:/home/node/.claude:z" \
  sandbox-image
```

**Networking penalty**: Rootless networking peaks at 2-4 Gbps vs Docker's 8-10 Gbps due to user-space netavark/pasta stack (discovery). Irrelevant for coding agents whose bottleneck is LLM API latency, not local network throughput.

## Firecracker MicroVMs

Industry consensus is forming: for truly untrusted agent code, microVMs are the correct isolation unit [1][2]:

- **Boot**: ~125ms from scratch; 28ms with snapshot/restore [3][37]
- **Overhead**: <5 MiB per VM; 150 VMs/second/host throughput [3]
- **Isolation**: Dedicated kernel per workload; kernel vulnerabilities in one VM cannot affect others [1]
- **Production users**: AWS Lambda, AWS Fargate, E2B (15M sessions/month) [32]

The 2024-2025 runc CVE cluster (CVE-2024-21626, CVE-2025-31133, CVE-2025-52565) drove adoption toward Firecracker for agent workloads (discovery). Containers share the host kernel — a kernel vulnerability means container escape. MicroVMs eliminate this class entirely.

## gVisor

Google's user-space kernel provides a middle ground [4]:

- **Architecture**: Go-written "Sentry" intercepts all syscalls; host kernel never sees application syscalls directly [4]
- **Performance**: 10-30% overhead on I/O-heavy workloads; minimal on compute tasks [1]
- **Default for K8s Agent Sandbox**: Google selected gVisor as the default runtime for the Kubernetes Agent Sandbox CRD [5]
- **GPU support**: Added for AI/ML workloads (negligible overhead claimed) [4]

Weaker than microVMs against kernel-level exploits but significantly stronger than plain containers. The right choice when you need better-than-container isolation but cannot afford microVM boot overhead or operational complexity.

## Kata Containers

Hardware-virtualized lightweight VMs conforming to OCI container APIs [2][5]:

- **From Kubernetes' perspective, it's a normal container. Under the hood, it's a full VM with hardware isolation** [1]
- **IBM use case**: Runs untrusted code in multitenant AI services (MCP servers, agent-generated code) (discovery)
- **Kata + Confidential Containers (CoCo)**: Cryptographic attestation for AI workloads in public cloud (discovery)
- **Formally integrated** with Google's Kubernetes Agent Sandbox alongside gVisor [5]

## Kubernetes Agent Sandbox (SIG Apps)

Purpose-built CRD for AI agent workloads on Kubernetes [5]:

```yaml
apiVersion: agentsandbox.io/v1
kind: Sandbox
metadata:
  name: agent-workspace
spec:
  runtime: gvisor  # or: kata
```

Key features:
- **SandboxWarmPool**: Pre-provisioned pods eliminate cold start (<1s claim) [5]
- **SandboxClaim**: Declarative API to obtain a pre-warmed sandbox [5]
- **Lifecycle**: Idle-to-active transitions, zero-resource scaling, state preservation across suspend/resume [5]
- **Stable networking**: Each sandbox gets stable hostname for multi-agent coordination [5]

## Cloud Sandbox Platforms

**E2B** [32]: Firecracker-backed, 80ms cold start, open-source, $21M raised. Adopted by Hugging Face, Perplexity, ~50% of Fortune 500 for agent workloads. Docker MCP Catalog integration (200+ tools).

**Daytona** [46]: Pivoted Feb 2025 to AI code execution. Default Docker (shared kernel) with optional Kata/Sysbox. <90ms launch. Less isolation than E2B by default.

**Cloudflare Dynamic Workers** (April 2026): V8 isolate-based sandboxing. 100× faster and 100× more memory-efficient than containers (claimed). Limited to JavaScript/WASM workloads (discovery).

## Selection Guidance

| Scenario | Recommended Isolation | Rationale |
|----------|----------------------|-----------|
| Trusted agent, own code, dev workstation | Podman rootless + --cap-drop ALL | Fast, sufficient for non-adversarial code [24][43] |
| Semi-trusted agent, multi-tenant | gVisor | Syscall interception without VM overhead [1][4] |
| Untrusted agent, arbitrary code execution | Firecracker or Kata | Hardware boundary prevents kernel exploits [1][2][3] |
| Kubernetes cluster, multiple agents | K8s Agent Sandbox (gVisor or Kata) | Declarative, warm pools, lifecycle management [5] |
| Rapid prototyping, no infra team | E2B or Managed Agents | Someone else manages the boundary [25][32] |

## Gaps and Limitations

- **gVisor syscall coverage**: ~70-80% of Linux syscalls supported [2]. Agents using exotic syscalls may fail silently.
- **Firecracker compatibility**: Limited virtual devices (network, block, serial) means no USB, GPU passthrough, or complex I/O (discovery).
- **Kata startup**: ~200ms is meaningfully slower than container startup for high-frequency agent invocations [2].
- **Nix/Devbox**: Provides dependency isolation, not kernel isolation — no container escape protection (discovery).
